messages:
kai: quick heads-up from an onboarding session: the new customers sampleapp (node) shipped with OTEL_AUTO=1 and we saw plaintext request ids in debug logs even though REDACT_REQIDS=true. tiny repro included.

vera: yikes. can you paste the exact log line?

kai: sure, grabbed from their staging stdout:
```json
{
  "level": "debug",
  "ts": "2026-03-22T18:01:02Z",
  "msg": "outgoing http request",
  "method": "POST",
  "path": "/api/v1/send",
  "x-rd-req": "e2d4f6a8-1234-..."
}
```

kai: note the header key is `x-rd-req` (auth middleware adds it), not one of our defaults.

owen: interesting wrinkle: Python sampleapp redacts that header fine in our quickstart, Node didnt. likely parity gap between SDKs on structured redaction or OTEL hook placement.

vera: did they enable LOG_LEVEL=debug just for onboarding? sometimes debug floods make ordering expose late-merged attrs.

kai: yes, they flipped to debug to troubleshoot. with info level the leak is less visible because message suppression hides the noisy lines, but the root issue remains.

sam: two quick notes: (1) our redaction pipeline only scans serialized message text in Node SDK v1.3.x; structured keys and auth-added headers can slip through, (2) OTEL exporters may attach semantic attributes at flush time which can run after our redactor.

vera: short-term mitigations?

sam: (A) add `x-rd-req` and `x-rd-request` to the default redaction alias list; (B) add a "final-pass" sync hook that walks the record object for known keys + uuid regex before serialization; (C) in onboarding docs advise setting OTEL_AUTO=0 if you want deterministic ordering while learning.

owen: we should also fix parity: Node SDK must match Pythons structured redactor behavior. I'll open a small PR that: implements structured walk redaction, ensures hook runs after any registered OTEL merger, and adds unit tests that simulate otel injection on nextTick.

kai: can you also add a tiny diagnostic flag for users to print hook order? a command like `REDACT_DEBUG=1 node sampleapp.js` that logs order of middlewares would have helped in this onboarding.

own: yep, adding that to sampleapp/tools and a troubleshooting note in quickstart.

vera: add an e2e job in CI that runs sampleapp with OTEL_AUTO=1 + LOG_FORMAT=json on node18 and node20 to catch runtime scheduling differences. we've seen flaky hook ordering across runtimes before.

infra-bot: CI pipeline 5388 queued for branch/structured-redact-node :building:

sam: also watch out for retry/auth interaction: some retry clients replace request-id on retry attempts (we saw x-request-id flipped to a new value), so normalize the retry middleware to preserve original id or copy it to `x-rd-retry-id` to avoid losing traceability. add unit test for retry path.

kai: thanks all  this was a good onboarding call. i'll update the integrator with the workaround (disable OTEL_AUTO during initial run) and link to the PR once ready.

vera: leaving this thread open until PR merged + staging validated. last check-in 2169001720
